skills.name: Conservation of mass and types of change

note.text:
In every change, physical or chemical, matter is not created or destroyed.
• Physical change (melting, dissolving, freezing): the mass stays the same. Ice of mass 50 g melts to 50 g of water.
• Chemical change in a closed container: the total mass of the products equals the total mass of the reactants.
• In an open container a gas may escape, so the mass seems to go down (burning wood, heating limestone); or a gas from the air may join, so the mass seems to go up (burning magnesium, rusting iron). The atoms are still all there.
Mass of reactants = mass of products.

worked_example.problem: {a} g of calcium carbonate is heated. {b} g of calcium oxide is left. What mass of carbon dioxide escaped?
steps: Mass of reactants = mass of products.

cards.idea: In a physical change the mass stays the same.
example: Ice melts: the water has the same mass as the ice.
Sugar dissolved in tea adds its mass to the tea.

cards.idea: In a chemical change the total mass of the products equals the total mass of the reactants.
example: Iron + sulphur in a closed tube: the mass does not change.

check.prompt: {a} g of iron and {b} g of sulphur react completely in a closed tube. What is the mass of iron sulphide formed?

misconceptions.explain: Nothing escapes from a closed tube: add the masses.

solution: Mass of products = mass of reactants.

cards.idea: In an open container a gas can escape (mass seems to fall) or oxygen from the air can join (mass seems to rise).
example: Burning wood: smoke and gases escape.
Burning magnesium: oxygen joins, the ash is heavier.

pick.q: Magnesium ribbon is burned in an open crucible. Why is the ash heavier than the magnesium?
pick.r: Oxygen from the air has joined the magnesium.
w: Mass was created in the reaction.
pick.y: Magnesium + oxygen → magnesium oxide: the oxygen adds mass.

pick.q: A piece of wood is burned in the open. Why is the ash lighter than the wood?
pick.r: Gases and smoke escaped into the air.
w: The ash is a different element.
Wood has no mass when dry.
e: The ash is not lighter for that reason.
pick.y: The products include gases that escaped.

questions.prompt: {m} g of ice melts completely. What is the mass of the water formed?
solution: The mass stays the same: {answer} g.
